Subject: RiverMark compliance gating: runtime audit-tags & residency guarantee request

Team —

Quick context: RiverMark (large regional bank) is at final commercial review. Procurement/legal have two gating asks that are currently blocking signature:

1) Per-request audit tags that are stored with each inference (customer-provided tag + internal trace id) and surfaced in the audit export used for compliance reviews. They need the tags to be immutable and retained for 24 months.

2) A residency guarantee for a pinned model variant for a limited tenant pool (RiverMark) — they want a residency SLA so that a selected model variant remains resident/warmed on a dedicated pool to limit cold-start variance during peak hours. They asked for a measurable SLO in the SOW (p95 inference time under the pinned pool for requests <512 tokens).

They've shared an initial SOW and a completed security questionnaire (attached). Procurement is asking for an engineering estimate and a go/no-go by EOW (2026-08-21) to keep the current discount band.

Ask: can PM/Eng (Karthik/Dev/Marcus) please review the attached materials and respond with:
- feasibility summary for both asks (audit tags + residency SLA),
- a proposed minimal viable rollout (what we can ship in 1 sprint to unblock contract),
- high level implementation effort (story points or rough sprint counts) and major blockers (cost, infra, security reviews),
- risk/impact bullet (cost delta estimate or required infra changes).

If it's easier, propose a 30m sync early next week; RiverMark is happy to be on a short call.

Thanks — this is a high ACV, high-sensitivity pilot; we should keep legal/solutions closely informed.

— Stephanie

Subject: Re: RiverMark compliance gating: runtime audit-tags & residency guarantee request

Thanks for the heads-up, Steph. Reviewed the SOW at a high level — sensible ask but two different workstreams. A few clarifying Qs before I commit estimates: 

1) For the audit tags: are RiverMark expecting us to accept arbitrary customer tags (free text) per request, or a constrained schema? Will they include PIIs? The retention and immutability requirements mean we need storage + retention policies + query/export support.

2) For residency: are they asking for dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) for RiverMark only, or are they OK with a soft "pinning" model where we bias routing and keep a warmed cache? The former is much more expensive but simpler SLO modeling; the latter is lower cost but harder to guarantee under high cluster churn.

Preliminary thoughts:
- Audit-tags MVP (1 sprint): header propagation + write-through in request logs and a new export field. Risk: retention and legal review for storage of customer-provided tags.
- Residency MVP (2-3 sprints if we do a soft pin): implement route-level residency hints + warmup policy + metrics dashboard. True dedicated-residency with capacity reservation + billing model will likely be 6+ sprints and will need Product + Sales/Revenue to sign off on pricing implications.

I can put together a short tech spike/update doc tomorrow. Dev — can you weigh in on the perf impact / storage estimate? Marcus — will need your read on customer-facing SLO wording and contract language implications.

If this is blocking the discount band, we should prioritize the audit tags quick-win first. Happy to take this to the roadmap prioritization forum but would prefer a short triage sync.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP Product | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RiverMark compliance gating: runtime audit-tags & residency guarantee request

Karthik / Steph / team — quick technical scope from infra/runtime side.

Audit tags: implementation plan and rough estimates
- Option A (MVP, 1 sprint): Accept a defined header (X-RM-Audit-Tag) that we propagate through the request path and write to the existing request log record (adds ~40 bytes per request). Add a new column in the export pipeline and surface in the audit export. Work items: header parsing + log ETL change + docs + legal signoff on retention. Risk: if customers send large free-text blobs we need strict length limit and validation.
- Option B (robust, 3-4 sprints): Schema support + indexing + search for tags (for their auditors) + retention UI. Higher infra cost for index/store.

Residency: feasibility notes
- Soft pin (preferred short-term): routing hint to bias requests to a pool and proactive warmup (cache pre-seeding). Changes required: routing policy flag, warmup worker, residency metrics. Can be delivered as an opt-in feature and tested with a single tenant. Estimated effort: 2 sprints for core pieces + 1 sprint for observability and rollout controls.
- Dedicated pool (long-term): provisioning, billing changes, capacity reservation, admission control. This ties into Dedicated product and will require infra budget and SRE onboarding — estimate 6+ sprints and procurement/finance coordination.

Perf impact: Option A adds negligible latency (<1ms) to happy-path; indexing (Option B) could add tail amplification on writes. Residency warmup increases GPU usage (cost delta depends on desired warm pool size). I can assemble a back-of-envelope cost for a pinned 4-GPU pool for RiverMark.

Next steps I propose:
- Ship Option A for audit tags as a toggle (1 sprint) — unblocks contract.
- Ship Soft Pin residency as a pilot (2-3 sprints) with RiverMark as canary tenant; measure p95 and iterate toward a formal SLA if behavior stabilizes.

I can scope a ticket set and propose sprint-by-sprint breakdown by EOD today.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime Team | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik/Dev — this is perfect.

Two quick confirmations from RiverMark (Julia replied on thread):
- They can accept a constrained header (X-RM-Audit-Tag) with a 256 char limit for the pilot. They don't plan to send PII in that header for the pilot (legal confirmed).
- They're happy to proceed with a soft pin pilot as long as we provide a short results report after 2 weeks of pilot traffic.

Action items we want to capture:
- Dev: create a ticket for Option A (audit header) and target the toggle-on for the next sprint (Sprint 27). Please include ETL export column in the scope and a short retention policy note for Legal.
- Dev/Karthik: scope the soft-pin pilot and provide a pilot runbook (warmup keys, metrics to capture, rollback plan). Target: pilot in Sprint 28 if feasible.
- Marcus: I'll loop you in on contract language to ensure the SOW reflects "soft-pin pilot" and not a firm capacity reserved SLA. Legal will want this distinction.

RiverMark noted procurement wants an official sign-by date of 2026-08-28 to keep the negotiated commercial terms. If we can commit to the audit-header quick-win and the pilot schedule, they will proceed to signature and start the PoC.

I'll update HubSpot and attach the signed SOW stub after signature. Thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround.
